clue.text: Lovely crowd, and God-fearing — about time

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly crowd, as in a scrum of reporters

indicators.note: the devout word goes about, around, the letter for time

parts.note: pious means devout, God-fearing

explanation.surface: A description of a pleasant, religious congregation that keeps an eye on the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovely crowd' looks like one phrase, but Lovely alone is the definition; a scrum, the rugby huddle, also means a jostling crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumptious is an informal word for delicious or delightful, a synonym of lovely.

clue.text: Lycra's hope to contain collapse

indicators.note: the phrase Lycra's hope holds the answer within its letters, running across the word break

explanation.surface: Someone hoping their stretchy Lycra garment will hold in a sagging figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a sudden collapse, whether of a market, a computer or a structure.

clue.text: City abandoning cleaner strip

indicators.note: the cleaner's word leaves behind, abandons, the letters of the city

parts.note: a laundress is a woman who washes clothes, a cleaner
LA is Los Angeles, the city

explanation.surface: A cleaner quitting the city to take up stripping.
explanation.walkthrough: LA (Los Angeles) is taken from the front of LAUNDRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To undress and to strip are synonymous verbs for taking off one's clothes.

clue.text: Sort of English message bearer broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the bird's name is said aloud

parts.note: a carrier pigeon bears messages

explanation.surface: A messenger whose broadcast is in a simplified kind of English.
explanation.walkthrough: PIGEON and PIDGIN sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Pidgin English is a simplified contact language mixing English with local tongues, so it is a sort of English.

clue.text: Popular view has answer for first of international's attack

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the answer's letter stands for, replaces, that opening letter

parts.note: a vision is a view or sight

indicators.note: the opening letter of international's is taken

explanation.surface: A popular perspective on an international dispute turning to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'first of international's' is not taken into the answer: it names the letter that the answer's A displaces.
explanation.definitionFit: An invasion is an armed incursion into another country, a form of attack.

clue.text: Just by winning post

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: up means ahead, winning, as in two goals up
right means just or fair

explanation.surface: Someone who has just squeaked past the winning post in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning post' reads as the finishing line, but post alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a vertical post, such as one of the posts of a goal.

clue.text: A 10 when eating escargot that's tough

parts.note: the answer to 10 Across is SHARD

indicators.note: the word for when takes in, eats, the snail

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
escargot is French for snail

explanation.surface: A fragment found while eating snails that turned out to be chewy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 points to the answer of 10 Across; 'escargot' is the French culinary word, giving the English creature.
explanation.definitionFit: As hard as nails is an idiom for someone very tough and unsentimental.

clue.text: Promise to support father, keeping nothing and do without

indicators.note: in a down clue the promise sits below, supporting, the first part
the father's letters keep, hold, the nothing inside them

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
O is zero, nothing
to swear is to promise solemnly

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to look after their father while giving things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To forswear is to renounce or give up something, so to abstain from it or do without.

clue.text: Intolerable and badly done by, help team lacking millions

indicators.note: badly means in a disordered way, so the letters are rearranged
the word team goes without, lacks, the letter for millions

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that the help team has treated them intolerably.
explanation.walkthrough: Team without M is TEA; DONEBYHELPTEA is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond the pale is an idiom for conduct outside the bounds of acceptable behaviour, unacceptable.

clue.text: Second difficult piece

parts.note: hard means difficult

explanation.surface: A second awkward fragment to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a broken fragment of glass or pottery, a sharp piece.

clue.text: Fish lovers do upset me, ultimately

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, disordered, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of me is taken

explanation.surface: A seafood fan complaining that couples in love irritate them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a flatfish prized in European cooking, named after the English port.

clue.text: Chalet is planned to accommodate leader of team sport

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, accommodate, the team's leader
planned means arranged, so these letters are put into a new order
the leader of team is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ski chalet being designed to house the captain of a sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: CHALETIS rearranged, with T put inside, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletics is the sport of running, jumping and throwing events on track and field.

clue.text: Zest left of oranges after sudden blow

indicators.note: the orange's letter comes after the gust

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind

indicators.note: the left-hand end of oranges in an across clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Orange zest left behind after a gust of wind blows the fruit away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zest' and 'oranges' suggest peel, but zest here means enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto and zest are synonyms for hearty enjoyment and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Backing crazy demand for material

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for crazy is reversed

parts.note: mad means crazy
to ask is to demand, as in 'asking a price'

explanation.surface: Supporting an unreasonable demand for fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned fabric, often of silk or linen, so a kind of material.

clue.text: Support from mother during visit?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
in means during, as in 'in the night'
a stay is a visit

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a mother's visit will bring help.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is a chief support, originally the rope steadying a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Quiet about unfashionable demise for resort

indicators.note: the quiet letters go about, around, the unfashionable word

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
out means out of fashion
demise means end

explanation.surface: A seaside town quietly going out of fashion and dying.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend-on-Sea is an English seaside resort in Essex, east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Southend is a seaside holiday town on the Thames estuary, a classic English resort.

clue.text: New branch of force facing initially serious riot

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of serious is taken

parts.note: a riot, like a hoot, is something hilarious

explanation.surface: A new wing of the police force confronting a serious riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' suggests disorder for the police, but here it means something very funny, a hoot.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a new shoot from a plant's stem, or something that branches off from an organisation.

clue.text: Bargains rejected must include cancelled by-products

indicators.note: the reversed bargains must contain the cancelled word
rejected means thrown back, so the word for bargains is reversed

parts.note: a snip is a bargain, something cheap
off means cancelled, as in 'the match is off'

explanation.surface: A rule that sale goods include discontinued side products.
explanation.walkthrough: A snip is British slang for a bargain, something surprisingly cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin-offs are incidental products or benefits arising from a main activity, by-products.

clue.text: Busy working even if drinking for example

parts.note: on means working, functioning, as in a machine that is on

indicators.note: the word for even if takes in, drinks, the example letters

parts.note: tho is an informal spelling of though, meaning even if
EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone still working even while having a drink, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: On the go is an idiom for constantly active, so busy.

clue.text: Burn church following endless derision

indicators.note: the church letters follow, come after, the trimmed derision
endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: scorn means derision

explanation.surface: A church being set on fire after constant mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to burn the surface of something, a mild form of burning.

clue.text: Container clue designed to cover a note

indicators.note: the rearranged clue letters go round, cover, the a and note
designed means arranged or made into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: A crossword clue written to conceal a hidden message.
explanation.walkthrough: CLUE rearranged as CULE goes around APS.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule is a small case or container, such as a time capsule or a pill casing.

clue.text: Game of cards may see skipper here!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the trick-taking card game for four players
second meaning: a ship's ..., the platform where the captain stands

explanation.walkthrough: Skipper sounds like a card player's partner, but it is a ship's captain on the command platform.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a partnership card game and the raised command deck from which a captain directs a ship.

clue.text: A second place is a plus

parts.note: to set is to place, put down

explanation.surface: Coming second, a runner-up place, still counts as a good result.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable quality, an advantage or plus.

clue.text: Refuse to be seen here in refurbished C&A perhaps

indicators.note: refurbished means renovated, done up anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C&A is a clothing chain store; the ampersand is ignored, leaving C and A

explanation.surface: Someone declining to be spotted in a done-up branch of a cheap clothing store.
explanation.walkthrough: C&A was a budget clothing chain once on British high streets. 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a pile of discarded waste, where rubbish or refuse ends up.

clue.text: Supply drug (crack)

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a crack is a joke or wisecrack, a quip

explanation.surface: Supplying crack cocaine as a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' in brackets looks like naming the drug, but it means a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to supply or furnish someone with what they need.

clue.text: Relax grip on Liberal form of tenure

indicators.note: in an across clue the relaxed grip comes on, after, the Liberal letter

parts.note: to ease is to relax or loosen
a hold is a grip

explanation.surface: Advice to a Liberal politician to loosen their grip on property.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasehold is a way of holding property for a fixed term under a lease, as opposed to freehold.

clue.text: Typical American university: all on vacation!

parts.note: US stands for United States, American

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so all keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An American university emptied because everyone is on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday, but it empties all of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual means normal or customary, the same as typical.

clue.text: Shifting to centre, politicians clash

indicators.note: shifting means moving around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament, politicians

explanation.surface: Politicians clashing as they shift to the centre ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A contretemps is a minor dispute or awkward disagreement, a clash.
